findings.title: Allocating call (GetBuffer()) inside DisallowGarbageCollection scope in Uint8ArrayToBase64
findings.message: In Uint8ArrayToBase64 (later renamed Uint8ArrayPrototypeToBase64), the expression `uint8array->GetBuffer()->backing_store()` is called inside a `DisallowGarbageCollection no_gc;` scope. `GetBuffer()` returns a Handle<JSArrayBuffer> which may require heap allocation to materialize the JSArrayBuffer object. Performing such an allocation while GC is explicitly disallowed triggers a V8 DCHECK failure: `AllowGarbageCollection::IsAllowed()` in heap.cc. The fix is to use `uint8array->DataPtr()`, which directly returns the raw data pointer of the typed array without any heap allocation.

location.snippet:
size_t simd_result_size = simdutf::binary_to_base64(
        std::bit_cast<const char*>(uint8array->GetBuffer()->backing_store()),
        uint8array->byte_length(),
        reinterpret_cast<char*>(output->GetChars(no_gc)), alphabet);

findings.suggestion: Replace `uint8array->GetBuffer()->backing_store()` with `uint8array->DataPtr()`. The DataPtr() accessor returns the typed array's data pointer directly as a raw pointer without performing any heap allocation, making it safe to call inside a DisallowGarbageCollection scope.

ground_truth.root_cause: The developer incorrectly used `GetBuffer()->backing_store()` to retrieve the raw byte pointer of a TypedArray's backing store inside a GC-disallowed scope. `GetBuffer()` returns a Handle<JSArrayBuffer> which may require heap allocation (e.g., to materialize a lazily-created buffer). The correct approach is to use `DataPtr()`, which directly returns the raw data pointer from the typed array object itself without any allocation.
